appraisal_events.evidence: Mme de Villebon's weekly snubs of Mme G... 'ne fut pas tout à fait inutile': in Mme G...'s eyes they endowed Mme de Villebon with a prestige 'd'ailleurs purement imaginaire' so great that, when Mme G...'s daughter came to be married, she astonishingly refused every duke, her mother wanting for her only 'un fils Villebon.'
appraisal_events.explanation: Mme de Villebon's persistent, contemptuous snubbing of Mme G... paradoxically produces an outsized, wholly imaginary prestige in the very woman she scorns, with real downstream consequences for a marriage choice.

appraisal_events.evidence: Told 'Swann est plus jeune que Palamède,' Mme de Gallardon retorts, 'Du moins il vous le dit; et s'il vous le dit soyez sûr que c'est qu'il y trouve son intérêt,' impugning his honesty.
appraisal_events.explanation: A passing quoted remark casts doubt on Swann's truthfulness, though the narrator frames it as symptomatic of reflexive Courvoisier suspicion toward anyone merely clever rather than well-born, softening its force.

status_effects.explanation: Her sustained snobbery is shown, ironically, to have won her an inflated prestige in Mme G...'s private estimation, with concrete effect on a marriage decision.
A quoted remark casts mild doubt on his honesty, though the narrator's ironizing frame around Courvoisier suspicion tempers the force of the insinuation.
